nodes.title: Block-pocket corner foam stress read as vm(L/2), L = (1/pi)(K_Ic/sigma_0)^2 (D-153)
nodes.text: Foam-only volume average over a ball of radius L/2 = 1.78 mm, maximised over the ball centre (the 3000 highest foam elements tried as centres), compared with the unchanged allowables
nodes.basis: the corner is a bimaterial singularity (Williams exponents 0.255 / 0.30, c2r5_wedge.py), so any peak or fixed sub-L average grows with refinement; for those exponents the ball average reads the point-method stress at about 0.35 L, more conservative than the point (0.5 L) and line methods; sigma_0 is the highest strength on record (shortest L). nodes.title: Fin root bond break from x 0.22 to the TE (design, closure round)
nodes.text: From x 0.22 (30 mm ahead of the elevon hinge, 10 R ahead of the cut-out corners) to the TE, under each half-fin root (4 places), two overlapping 25.4 mm strips of PTFE film tape (about 45 mm wide, centred on the fin plane) are laid on the wing skin before the root bond; the root edge, its 13 mm coves and the fin's 15 mm skin-tape laps sit on it and bond to the fin only. Ahead of the hinge the root, coves and laps bond as drawn
nodes.basis: epoxy and packing-tape adhesive do not bond to PTFE (a release surface); 45 mm covers the two 13 mm cove legs, the root edge and 8 mm of margin each side, so no epoxy or lap reaches the wing skin aft of x 0.22. Mass about 4.9 g for the four roots (EST: 3.5 mil PTFE + silicone adhesive, about 0.24 kg/m2, 8 strips x 100 x 25.4 mm). The break sits 30 mm ahead of the hinge because a bonded root ending at the hinge line loads the cut-out corners (closure-round runs: corner compression 118.7 kPa vs 120 at local level 2, rising with refinement; 75.9 with the break at 0.22)

nodes.title: Fin root fillet load = C4's fillet-intact split, aft share moved ahead of the bond break (rigid root)
nodes.text: The bonded half-fin root and coves carry, per quarter, the force and moment C4 computed with the root pinned (team/C4/claims.d3.json CALC-C4-D3-STATIC fillet_share_table, L4 and G2, both senses, limit); the share C4 puts aft of x 0.22 is moved, with its moment, onto the bonded root ahead of x 0.22 (ASM-C2-FILLET-BREAK); the block carries the rest of the station load
nodes.basis: a pinned (rigid) root attracts the most load; the real root sits on foam and sheds load back to the tube / block path, so the split is an upper bound for the fillet; moving the aft share forward (rather than back to the block) is the larger load on the bonded root. C4's table is for the shoe before D-106 (C4 to re-issue it on the drawn shoe with the root free aft of the hinge)

The fin is fixed to the tube and the through-core block, which is far stiffer than a microballoon cove on foam, so the bonded fillet carries only what compatibility gives it; C4 computed that split with the root pinned (rigid, an upper bound: CR-C2-12 answer, CL-C4-D3-FILLET-L4-SHARE 0.73 % of the root moment). nodes.title: Core foam shear if the fin root fillet carried 100 % of the station loads (not a reachable state, record)
nodes.how: Bounding record; the real path is CL-C2-FEA-SPLIT-S1 / -TAU
nodes.note: record, no limit (closure round 2026-11-14): 100 % of the station loads through the fin root fillet is not a state the drawn wing can reach. The fin is fixed to the tube and the through-core block, which is far stiffer than a microballoon cove on foam, so the bonded fillet carries only what compatibility gives it; C4 computed that split with the root pinned (rigid, an upper bound: CR-C2-12 answer, CL-C4-D3-FILLET-L4-SHARE 0.73 % of the root moment). The real path is checked with C4's split in CL-C2-FEA-SPLIT-* and CL-C2-FEA-CUTOUT-SPLIT-*. A 100 % path needs the block path gone (a broken block), which T-C4-BLOCK-PROOF and CL-C2-FEA-PETG cover
